summary: Shoji Mori specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Toyo University and under Giyu Nishi (~1962–1971). His career included posts at The Okurayama Institute (~1971) and Toyo University as associate professor (~1979–1988) and professor (~1988–2008).
Shoju Inaba worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts as professor at Otani University (~1957–1980) and part-time lecturer at Nagoya University.
Shojun Bando was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1951–1956). He held academic posts at Ueno Gakuen University (~1960–1999) and Otani University (~1975–1997).

Shokin Furuta studied Buddhist studies and philosophy at Matsue High School, University of Tokyo, Tokyo University of Education, and Shimane University, studying under Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki. He held professorships at Hokkaido University (~1952–1964) and Nihon University (~1964–1981).
Shoko Kanaoka was a scholar in sinology and Buddhist studies. He held a professorship at Toyo University, where his posts are attested in 1987 and 2000.

Shoko Miyabayashi studied Buddhist studies at Taisho University (1948–~1955). He spent his academic career at Taisho University as a lecturer (1960), associate professor (1962), and Dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (1978–2002).

Shoko Miyata works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Miyata's affiliations include lecturer posts at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, attested in 2026.
Shoko Takeuchi specialized in Buddhist studies, studying at Ryukoku University. Takeuchi later served as professor emeritus at Ryukoku University, attested between 1987 and 1995.

Shoko Watanabe studied Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University under Ernst Leumann and Naoshiro Tsuji. Posts included professor at Taisho University (1935–1943) and Toyo University (1956–1969).

Shoku Bando studied Buddhist studies and Indology at Kyoto University of Education, Otani University, and the University of Freiburg. In 1987, Bando held posts at the Abhidharma Research Institute, Kyoto University, and Fukui Prefectural College.

Shoryu Katsura studied Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy at Kyoto University and the University of Toronto under A. K. Warder and others. Posts included professor at Hiroshima University (1976–2004) and Ryukoku University (2004–2015).

Shoshin Fukihara studied Buddhist studies at Otani University and Horyu-ji under Susumu Yamaguchi and Join Saeki. Main posts included professor at Shinshu College, associate professor at Doho University, and professor at Otani University Junior College (~1963–1973).

Shoshin Kuwayama focused on history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Kyoto University (~1958–1967), Kuwayama served there as assistant professor (~1972–1989) and professor emeritus (~1989–2002) at the Institute for Research in Humanities.

Shoshun Hayashidera specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Hayashidera held a post at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2011) and serves as professor at Hokkaido University (attested 2026).

Shoson Miyamoto studied Buddhist studies and Indology at Otani, Tokyo, and Oxford universities. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1942), Toyo University (~1947–1952), Komazawa University (~1954–1973), and Waseda University (~1954–1964).
Shou-chien Shih works in history, archaeology, and sinology. Shih served as a professor at National Taiwan University (~1987) and as director of the National Palace Museum (~2000–2004).

Shoyu Hanayama studied Buddhist studies at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1953). Hanayama served as vice president of Musashino University (~1970–1995) and chairperson of Bukkyo D伝do Kyokai until 1995.

Shozen Kumoi studied Buddhist studies and Indology at Otani University and under Erich Frauwallner in Vienna (~1958–1960). Posts included associate professor at Otani University (1948–1981) and professor at Bukkyo University (1982).
Shri Krishna Saksena worked in philosophy and Indology, holding professorships at the University of Lucknow and the University of Hawaiʻi.
Shri Krishna Sharma was active in Indology and linguistics. Sharma founded the Hindu Maha Sabha and DAV College, Suva.
